response.reason: The cited clause (Art. 26(3) of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011) establishes the requirement that if the country of origin or place of provenance of a food is given and it differs from that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or it must be indicated that it is different. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that since both the food and its primary ingredient have the same origin (Norway), the requirement is satisfied. The clause is directly relevant and supports the legal grounding of the verdict.
